NSC.thesis_one_line: Eastern US freight railroad being bought by Union Pacific; the price mostly bets that regulators approve, and standalone it already prices strong growth.
kill_criteria: STB issues a final decision denying the UNP-NSC merger, or either party gives notice of termination.
NSC adjusted operating ratio above 67.0% for two consecutive quarters (company-defined adjusted basis, consolidated, quarterly release).
Consolidated debt-to-total capitalization (10-Q MD&A, consolidated) above 55%.
Incident accruals plus environmental liabilities (10-Q note, consolidated) increase by more than $300m in any 12-month period.
UNP share price below $240 while NSC trades above $300 (deal spread would then exceed 25%).
key_adverse_facts: STB rejected the first application as incomplete on 16 Jan 2026; revised application accepted 28 May 2026 but held in abeyance for supplemental information
H1 26 free cash flow about $577m vs about $1,103m; incident cash payments $322m
COO resigned for good reason on 31 May 2026 citing proposed operational changes
Eastern Ohio consent decree pending since Oct 2024 and Ohio AG case open
data_conflicts: Triage said not advanced as merger-arb; confirmed situation but verdict WATCH not REJECT
Yahoo earnings timestamp is a past date; next earnings date is an estimate
STB September 2026 rulings known only from web search, not opened in a filing
NSC.confidence_in_thesis: low - outcome hinges on a regulatory decision expected in 2027

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Standalone price implies about 6.5% ten-year FCF growth versus my 5% base; deal terms of 1 UNP share plus $88.82 give $362.61 versus $313.

NSC.scenario_basis: Start $313, TTM adj EPS $12.69, dividend $5.40; base = 60% deal closes (about 10.6%/yr via 1 UNP share plus $88.82 cash) and 40% standalone about 0%; bear = deal fails, 17x $14 EPS plus $11 fee; bull = deal closes with UNP at 21x $17 EPS.

ARE.thesis_one_line: Largest lab-space landlord for biotech, trading at under nine times cash earnings while carrying heavy debt and still needing to sell billions of assets.
kill_criteria: Completed 2026 dispositions below $1.0bn at 31 Dec 2026 (company supplemental, versus the $2.9bn midpoint of "dispositions, sales of partial interests, and other capital sources" guidance).
Net debt and preferred stock to Adjusted EBITDA (consolidated, quarter annualised) above 6.5x at 4Q26.
FFO per share as adjusted guidance (midpoint now "$6.40") cut below $6.20 for 2026, or 2027 guidance midpoint (due 2 Dec 2026) below $5.60.
Operating occupancy (operating properties, 10-Q/supplement) below 85% for two consecutive quarters.
A further common dividend reduction below $0.72 per quarter.
key_adverse_facts: Net debt and preferred to Adjusted EBITDA 7.0x vs 4Q26 target 5.6x-6.2x
Only $170.4m of $2.9bn midpoint dispositions completed by 3 Aug 2026
1H26 FFO per share $3.46 vs $4.63 (-25%); dividend cut 45% to $0.72
Securities class action filed 25 Nov 2025; $1.0bn 7.25% junior subordinated notes issued Aug 2026
data_conflicts: Triage called red flags disqualifying; dossier finds cheap valuation but agrees leverage and execution risk justify WATCH
Yahoo EBITDA and debt (aggregator) differ from 10-Q carrying amounts
4Q25 and 3Q25 FFO per share not extracted
ARE.confidence_in_thesis: low - depends on asset sale execution and lab demand

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. 8.6x run-rate FFO implies FFO falling about 2% per year indefinitely versus my flat base; the discount reflects leverage and execution risk.

ARE.scenario_basis: Start $49.93, run-rate FFO $5.80, dividend $2.88; base FFO about $5.6-5.8 at 9x plus dividends; bear FFO $4.8 at 7x; bull FFO $6.2 at 11x.

KDP.thesis_one_line: Dr Pepper and Keurig owner that just bought a global coffee company with debt, priced at about 14 times earnings ahead of a planned split into two companies.
kill_criteria: Management leverage ratio (consolidated, company-defined, pro forma) above 4.5x at 31 Dec 2026 or guidance for it withdrawn.
Full-year 2026 constant-currency adjusted EPS growth guidance cut below "low-double-digit" (company release).
U.S. Refreshment Beverages volume/mix growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters.
Keurig antitrust: any adverse judgment or settlement above $500m (10-Q litigation note).
Separation timetable slips beyond 30 June 2027, or the preferred is not retired or refinanced on announced terms.
key_adverse_facts: Total debt about $29.98bn and $4.5bn convertible preferred after JDE Peet's deal
U.S. Coffee adjusted operating income -24.7% in Q2 26
Antitrust plaintiffs claim more than $1.5bn; no loss accrued
Q2 26 GAAP EPS $0.04 vs adjusted $0.57 on integration costs
data_conflicts: Triage 6.7x net debt/EBITDA uses partial-year EBITDA; management states about 4.1x pro forma, not independently verifiable
Aggregator FCF $4.6bn and forward EPS $2.53 include full-year JDE and differ from reported figures
Triage cited a 4.5x leverage target; the Q2 26 release says about 4.1x
KDP.confidence_in_thesis: med - clean U.S. beverage growth but leverage and split unproven

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Price at about 14x 2026 adjusted EPS and 5.8% estimated FCF yield implies about 3% ten-year growth versus my base of 6-8% for three years then 4%.

KDP.scenario_basis: Start $31.95, 2026E adjusted EPS $2.27, dividend $0.92; base EPS growth 8% to $2.86 at 14x; bear $2.40 at 11x; bull $3.10 at 16x.
